hypothesis: Some spots keep melanocytes that make pigment but hand it over poorly.
supporting_observation: Cultured melanocytes from six IGH patients were larger with short, retracted dendrites and held more melanin than cells from six controls; p16, p21 and hp1 were higher in lesional skin.
source: Rani et al., Int J Dermatol 2018, doi:10.1111/ijd.13960 (abstract checked)
what_would_weaken_it: Paired tissue showing melanocytes are simply absent, with no pigment build-up inside the cells that remain.

hypothesis: Regaining pigment depends on how many working pigment cells remain or can be recruited.
supporting_observation: After gentle freezing, repigmented spots had more dopa-positive melanocytes than untreated spots but fewer than normal skin. A 2023 letter is titled 'Melanocytes in IGH disappear and are senescent'.
source: Ploysangam et al., J Am Acad Dermatol 1990, PMID 2229495 (abstract checked); Kim TH et al., J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol 2023, PMID 36394380 (no abstract; title only)
what_would_weaken_it: Baseline biopsies that fail to predict which spots respond. No archive linking baseline tissue to later outcome has been found.

hypothesis: Local tissue changes under the spot help explain why neighbouring skin behaves differently.
supporting_observation: Superficial dermal fibrosis in 18 of 20 paired biopsies. A conference abstract reports more dendritic cells and M2 macrophages and fewer T cells in lesional than paired non-lesional sections.
source: Arbache et al., Int J Dermatol 2022, PMID 35114009 (abstract checked); Alphonse et al., SID 2024 abstract 858 (abstract checked; patient count not stated)
what_would_weaken_it: The same differences appearing in sun-damaged skin without spots, which would make them a marker of damage and not a cause.

hypothesis: Early loss of the autophagy protein ATG7 drives melanocyte ageing in sun-exposed skin.
supporting_observation: ATG7 was reduced in UVB-aged melanocytes and in IGH skin; metformin restored autophagy and delayed senescence in cultured cells.
source: Kim JC et al., Br J Dermatol 2026;194(5):879-887, PMID 41453137 (abstract checked)
what_would_weaken_it: No human treatment data exist. A finding in cultured cells says nothing yet about repigmenting an existing spot.
